messages:
Rae: quick idea  we need a tiny bench teaser (email + landing) called the 'Pulse Bench'  focus: p50 reliability + bounded p99 + token economics. keep it snackable.

Omar: nice. hero thought: 'Set a steady pulse for inference' subhead: 'Real numbers on latency and token spend.' short & punchy.

Jules: visuals: 1) sparkline scatter: median latency (p50) vs cost/1k tokens, 2) mini GIF showing micro-batching in action (2-3s), 3) compact bar: p95 vs p99 with/without caching. each gets one plain-English takeaway.

Nikhil: copy: opener: "Stop guessing monthly token bills." then 3 bullets: what we ran, typical % savings, tail impact. keep body <=120 words.

Cate: routing: two CTAs in email -> 'Run a 5-min pulse' (sandbox) and 'Request a perf check' (enterprise). detect corporate domains to nudge the perf CTA but let users choose. capture company size buckets. UTMs: pulse_bench_v1 and variant=A/B.

Rae: subject A: 'Set a steady pulse for inference' B: 'How steady is your inference latency?' A/B test to 6k recipients.

Omar: eng deliverables: CSV for hosted vs dedicated, a 4-bit quantized row, prompt-mix breakdown. also export a tiny GIF for batching. ETA Wed noon. link to benchmark doc in footer. claims must be conservative.

Jules: creative note: keep charts legible at 360px; use alt text and short captions. GIF must be <500KB.

Nikhil: landing page: quick sandbox runner (paste prompt -> run) and a short form for perf check: name, email, company, size, reason. map to HS_FORM_PULSE and HS_FORM_PERF placeholders. flag enterprise leads in HubSpot when size>200.

Cate: metrics: open rate, click->sandbox %, demo-book %, webinar signups (if we run one), MQLs. set initial KPI: 10% click->sandbox for personal domains, 6% perf-check for corporate.

campaign-bot: Campaign scaffolded (id=camp_10221). Assets folder: https://drive.redwood/pulse-bench-10221. Test send scheduled 2025-01-10T17:00:00Z.

Rae: timeline: draft copy today, design + charts Tue, eng numbers Wed, LP/forms Thu, QA Fri, test send Mon. I'll drop the Drive copy now. keep claims tight and cite the detailed benchmark. :heartbeat:
